pages.name: Combat Is Risky and Dangerous
pages.html:
Combat Is Risky and Dangerous: Once weapons are drawn, someone is getting hurt. Keep in mind the following:

  • Death is final: NPCs are not willing to die over useless reasons or without any potential benefit. They want to stay alive.
  • No one wins in a gun fight: A single hit from a weapon can be debilitating. An exchange of attacks will harm both parties. Think before you shoot.
  • Reason over irrationality: If NPCs find themselves surrounded, cornered, or outnumbered, they are less likely to engage directly in violence if they deem it avoidable.

Time Frame

Time Frame: A combat round represents 10 seconds of time.

Book p.40

pages.name: Pre-Combat Set-up and Surprise
pages.html:
Pre-combat Set-up

  • Determine surprise.
  • Determine starting range distance between parties.
  • If a side achieves surprise, determine if the surprising party is able to escape or evade.

Surprise

Surprise: Surprise is used to determine who is able to either avoid combat or establish the combat in their favor. This roll is determined by one of the players for the character's side, while the referee rolls for the NPC side.

  • Determining surprise: Both sides roll 1D. If one side rolled 3 or more over their potential opponent’s die result, then that side gains surprise.
  • Gaining surprise: The side that gains surprise will then be able to determine if they want to escape, evade, or engage.
  • No surprise: If neither side gains surprise, then both parties are aware of each other.

Surprise rolls can be modified by the following table:

SkillDM
LeadershipLeadership rank
TacticsTactics rank
ReconRecon rank
Military Experience+1DM if anyone in the group was in the navy, marines, or army
  • A character that has Leadership 0 and Tactics 0 gains a +1DM.

Book p.40

pages.name: Range
pages.html:
Determine Encounter Range: If the range must be determined by the referee, then they roll on the Range Band table and modify their dice roll with the environmental DM. It is assumed all encounters are discovered at the furthest edge of the range band or as far as the environment allows within the determined range band.

2DRange Band
1 or lessClose
2-5Short
6-9Medium
10-11Long
12+Very long

  • Distance equivalent: This represents the distance per range band.
  • Example of weapon: This is the appropriate type of weapon that can be used at this range band.
  • Escape chance: This is the chance to escape combat before the encounter starts.

Environmental DMs: Use the following DMs to determine the range band.

EnvironmentDM

Book p.40

pages.name: Evade or Escape
pages.html:
• Evade: The side that gained surprise can choose to avoid the potential conflict without issue. If the NPCs gain surprise, the referee can dictate whether they engage or if they avoid by making a call or a roll of 8+ with an 8+ resulting in evading.
  • Escape: A side can still choose to avoid conflict. If a side desires to escape, they have to roll a 8+ to get away, modified by the range band table. However, once combat starts, a side can only retreat until the escaping group moves beyond the range of the opposing side's weapons or obstructs the opposing side from attack.

Book p.40

pages.name: The Combat Procedure
pages.html:
Once combat is certain, use the following steps to resolve a combat round:

Step 1) All Players Declare Their Actions in order of

  • A) Orders (If a character has Tactics)
  • B) Movement and positioning
  • C) Declare if they will attack or attempt a different Skill

Step 2) Resolve in Order

  • A) Movement resolution step: Characters and NPCs resolve moving simultaneously.
  • B) Attack step: Characters and NPCs resolve attacking or their declared Skill simultaneously.
  • C) Other action step: If any character or NPC has a non-combat or Skill action to perform, that is resolved simultaneously.

Step 3) End of the round

Once all participants finish their actions, the combat round is over.

  • Morale: If a side has 25% or more of their total starting numbers incapable of continuing to fight due to injury or death, make a morale check. Morale only affects NPCs.
  • Determine Continuation of Combat: If it is determined combat will continue, start a new combat round at step 1.

Book p.41

pages.name: Orders
pages.html:
Orders: A character can use their whole turn to provide orders before the start of the combat round

  • Give orders: A character with Tactics 0 can give orders to any and all NPCs on their side to act based on their commands, such as move, attack, overwatch, suppress, etc., each round they spend giving orders. Giving orders does not require a Skill roll.
  • Provide tactics: Any character with Tactics of rank 1 or more can apply a +DM at the beginning of each combat encounter equal to their Tactics rank or less to use, as long as the Tactics rank applies to the current encounter type each round. For example, Tactics (Starship) cannot be applied to a spacer on the ground.

Book p.41

pages.name: Movement and Carry Weight
pages.html:
Movement

Movement: Each player simultaneously moves their characters into position.

  • Movement distance: A character can move a number of metres equal to their current DEX score per combat round.
  • Terrain impact on movement: The referee may reduce the amount of distance they can travel based on the environment, such as if it's hard to navigate, cluttered, or on an incline. These rulings should reduce movement only up to a 1/2 reduction of movement from the terrain alone.

Carry Weight

Carry Weight: A character’s mobility may be impacted due to the amount they are carrying.

  • Minimal: A character can carry their x2 STR characteristic in kilograms without impact.
  • Encumbered: X3 STR in kilograms, reduce movement distance and combat endurance by 50%.
  • Over-Encumbered: x4 STR in kilograms, reduce movement by 75% and cannot sprint or make melee attacks.
  • Example: Dmitri has an STR of 8. He can carry up to 16kg without penalty but is considered encumbered if carrying between 17-24kg. Dmitri is over-encumbered if he carries 25-32kg and cannot make melee attacks or sprint.
  • Worn items: Clothing does not count towards weight, but when wearing armour or vaccsuits apply 50% of their weight to encumbrance.

Book p.41

pages.name: Positioning and Cover
pages.html:
Positioning: Characters should declare their positioning after movement to help give themselves protection from cover. Defender positioning and defender cover stack.

  • For example, a character kneeling behind half cover provides the attacker a -3DM to their attack roll.

Changing Positioning to Improve Cover: Sometimes a character can choose to change their positioning to have cover provide more defense. This will allow the cover to increase one step in the Defender positioning column.

  • For example: a standing character in partial cover grants -1DM to the attacker, but if they kneel then they gain -1DM from kneeling and the partial cover now functions as half cover, now providing -2DM. This allows for a total -3DM to the attacker.

Positioning table

Defender PositioningImpact to Attacker

Kneeling-1DM
Prone-2DM
Flat against Wall-1DM

Cover table

Defender CoverExample of CoverageImpact to Attacker
Partial Cover (25%)Knees and below-1DM

* Absolute Cover represents targets hiding behind cover that can be penetrated with a weapon. If the weapon cannot shoot through the cover, then the target is impossible to hit.

Changing Position and Movement: A character can only move up to 1/2 their maximum movement a round if they switch from kneeling, prone, or laying flat to movement. A character can only switch defensive positions once per round.

Book p.42

pages.name: Endurance in Combat
pages.html:
Endurance in Combat: A character's endurance is the measurement of a character's ability to sprint and attack with melee weapons during the encounter.

  • Sprinting: A character can run a number of extra metres past their DEX limit by using their END. However, they can only sprint a number of extra metres up to their END score per combat encounter.
  • Melee: A character can make a number of melee attacks equal to their END per combat encounter.
  • The player must track anytime their character sprints or uses melee.
  • END Damage: When injured, END is the first characteristic to be reduced. This will directly limit the number of remaining metres they may sprint or melee attacks they may make.

Book p.42

pages.name: Attacking
pages.html:
Attacking: On the attack step of the combat round, all related actions are assumed to occur simultaneously but are resolved in the following manner

  • 1) All attack rolls are made simultaneously.
  • 2) Any successful attacks then have damage applied.
  • 3) Determine who is incapacitated or killed.

Successful Attack: Characters that are attacking must beat the target’s armour difficulty to hit.

Determining a successful hit

Roll 2D + applicable Characteristic DM + Weapon Skill (if any) >/= Target’s Armour Difficulty.

  • The referee may rule which characteristic DM can be applied due to circumstances.
  • Aiming: A character using a ranged weapon is expected to aim their weapon, which takes the place of using a move action. If the character attempts to attack without aiming, they take -2DM for “shooting from the hip.”
  • Optional - Absolute Success: When two sixes are rolled (boxcars), then full weapon damage is applied to the target.
  • Optional - Absolute failure: When two ones are rolled (snake eyes), the gun is jammed or the blade is bent or broken. A gun can be unjammed on a successful Ranged combat roll with the relevant weapon, in place of an attack. A damaged blade cannot be used again until repaired outside of combat.
  • Untrained in a weapon: -3DM in place of a weapon Skill if using a weapon without any familiarity.
  • Weapon range: Weapons being used out of their range band will incur a penalty.
  • Missed Ranged Attacks: If an attack misses, then nothing happens.
  • Unintended target: if the target is engaged in melee with someone else or is positioned behind the intended target, there is a 50% chance that the unintended target is hit instead when a miss occurs. Make a second attack roll, modified by any environmental factors, to determine if it lands on the unintended target.

Book p.42

pages.name: Determining Damage
pages.html:
Damage: On a successful hit, roll weapon damage plus the effect of the successful attack roll to the damage. Melee weapons apply STR DM to damage.

  • Example of an attack roll: Dmitri is trained in using a blade, as indicated by Melee 0 (Blade 1). He uses a sword to attack an opponent in jack armor (9+ to hit) within short range, so he applies his DEX DM, which is +1, and his blade Skill, which is 1, for a total of +2. He then rolls 2D, which comes up as an 8. He applies the +2 and gets a 10. Success!
  • Example of a damage roll: Dmitri’s sword deals 2D damage. Because of his successful attack roll, he can roll 2D + STR DM (+0) + the success effect (+1) for damage. He rolls a 9 and adds +1 for 10, dealing 10 damage to the target’s END.

pages.name: Other Actions That Replace Attacking
pages.html:
• Evade: Any character that is moving during the round can also declare they are being evasive. That allows them to apply their DEX DM to their armour, but they cannot attack or perform a Skill that round.
  • Overwatch: A player can spend a whole round not moving or attacking to gain overwatch in the next combat round. This will allow the character to immediately attack any single target that moves within their line-of-sight during the movement step. For every full round spent in overwatch, apply a +1DM to the attack. Making an attack resets the overwatch attack DM to 0, but it can still increase again during the combat encounter. The DM can never be more than +5.
  • Use a Skill: A character can choose to use a Skill to help during the combat encounter, such as applying first aid (Medic), rally the morale of friendly NPCs (leadership), unjam a weapon (Ranged Combat), etc.

Book p.43

pages.name: Taking Damage
pages.html:
Taking Damage: When a character is damaged, it will be applied to their physical characteristics, starting with Endurance (END).

  • END is hit first: Damage is always applied to END first. If END reaches 0, the character is considered wounded and pinned in place. Excess damage from this attack is then applied equally to DEX and STR.
  • Additional hits: Additional damage is randomly applied to STR or DEX. Roll 1D: Odd results are STR; even results are DEX.

Injured Condition

Injured Condition: There are three categories of injury a character can have;

  • Wounded: When END reaches 0, the character is wounded and pinned in place and cannot move for the rest of combat without receiving first aid.
  • Unconscious: When a second physical characteristic reaches 0, the character is unconscious and cannot act.
  • Dead: When all three physical characteristics reach 0, the character is dead.

Book p.43

pages.name: Morale
pages.html:
Morale: Morale is determined by the referee in order to manage NPCs during stressful situations such as combat and survival. Morale is not used for the player characters. Morale can be used in a variety of situations where NPCs may react negatively to the circumstances, as determined by the referee.

  • General morale check: The referee rolls 2D; a result of 8+ is a success. If a character has the Leadership Skill, they instead make the roll and add their Leadership rank along with their SOC modifier.
  • Combat morale: When 25% of a side’s fighting strength is wounded, unconscious, pinned, or dead at the end of a round, they must roll 8+ to maintain rank and file.
  • Additional Morale Checks: The morale check is made again when 50% of the fighting strength decreases, but the roll is made at -2DM. At 25%, it is made at -4DM.

Book p.44

pages.name: Additional Combat Considerations
pages.html:
• Ambush: Being hidden allows for a single surprise attack, allowing the weapon to deal full weapon damage on a successful attack.
  • Attacking vehicles: If firing at a moving vehicle, apply their speed band as a -DM to the attack attempt. Any successful hit deals minimal weapon damage. See Vehicular Combat for more information.
  • Controlled melee attacks: Make a melee attack at -2DM to not have it count against the END limit.
  • Darkness: Using a weapon in darkness applies a -4DM in addition to any range penalties. The referee may choose to reduce this to -2 for low light or flickering lights.
  • Drawing weapon: Drawing a weapon uses a movement action during a combat round. It's assumed all characters have their weapons drawn at the start of combat unless stated otherwise.
  • Defending: Apply Weapon Skill rank as a negative DM to an attacker using melee attacks. This is applied automatically as long as the defender isn’t kneeling, prone, flat against a wall, or at END 0.
  • Higher ground: +2DM to attacks from any area significantly above the target.
  • Parry: Use an attack action to make a contested melee check. If you beat the attack, then make a free attack at +2DM. A parry can be made if the spacer hasn’t acted yet this round. A parry will use an additional point of endurance to perform.
  • Reload: Reloading a weapon takes one combat round but grants the reloading character Evade.
  • Suppression: Fire towards the location of an enemy to restrict their movement. 8+ to suppress. It causes the target to incur a negative to their armour equal to the effect, along with preventing them from moving or using an equipped weapon next round (pinned). Rolling an 8 means the target is only pinned.
  • Surrounding: The target’s armour difficulty to hit decreases by -1 per enemy flanking them from the side and behind within medium range or -2 per enemy within short range.
  • Zero-g combat: When fighting in zero-g, any melee or non-energy weapon attack will cause the character or NPC to move backwards from the direction of their attack. This movement is continuous until the character or NPC hits a surface or spends a round correcting themselves with a Vaccsuit Skill check of 8+. The distance the attacker moves is 1m per number of dice rolled. For example, shooting a body pistol will push back the attacker 2 metres. If attacking while in movement, apply the number of metres moved as a negative DM to any future attack rolls until the character or NPC stops moving.

Book p.44
